Deflection criterion: project ratio L/250.0 with effective absolute cap 15.000 mm. For overhangs the ratio uses the bearing spacing. This
project criterion is not a universal code limit.
End conditions in this analysis: start = pinned, end = pinned. Declared fixity does not verify the stiffness of the physical connection.
Gravity trial section screen only. Effective major-axis section resistance 49.14 kNm. Member buckling, shear resistance, local bearing,
torsion, connections and complete wind combinations require separate verification. The adopted displacement limit applies to the shortest

Prismatic Euler–Bernoulli elastic beam. Actual supports use a bending stiffness solver with zero bearing movement and independently
declared fixed/pinned/free ends; legacy intermediate bearings use compatibility. Diagram signs: positive V is the left-face convention;
positive M is sagging; negative displacement is downward. Full-span line actions, concentrated vertical forces and signed applied
support-transfer moments.
801 uniform stations, action/support boundaries and interior zero-shear candidates. Moment extrema include zero-shear candidates;
deflection maxima are sampled, not an exact root solve. Shear jumps retain separate left/right values. Torsion, shear deformation,
second-order effects and support settlement are excluded.
Equations: sum(R) = sum(P) + wL; sum(R*x) + sum(applied/support moments) = sum(P*x) + wL^2/2. dV/dx = -w; dM/dx = V;
EI*v_second_derivative = M, with the declared support boundary conditions. EI in kNm2 = E(MPa)*I(mm4)*1e-9. Report displacement is
converted to mm.

Load path, connections and verification register
Concurrent actions delivered to the support
Actions delivered by the beam to the support: local x along the span from start to end, y up, z out of the bending plane. Fy and Mz are the
negatives of the support reaction and counterclockwise support moment on the beam. Other components are not modelled; a blank is
unknown, not zero. These axes are not an assumed bolt-group coordinate system.
Connection component calculations are available under Steel connections and the project connection section. The trial provisions above do
not establish complete connection resistance. Competent structural engineering review is required before certification or fabrication.
R06 connection studies are partial checks. Member reactions alone do not constitute a verified concurrent six-component connection action
vector. Complete local member, plate, weld, bolt, anchor and joint checks remain necessary.
AS/NZS 1170.0:2002 | Structural design actions — General principles | Limit states and action combinations | Entered G/Q factors are
evaluated. Complete project combinations, robustness and project-adopted amendments require review. |
https://codehub.building.govt.nz/resources/1170-02002asnzs

occupancy, reduction rules and minimum prescribed loads are not independently verified. |
https://codehub.building.govt.nz/resources/1170-12002asnzsa2
AS/NZS 1170.2:2021 | Wind actions | Site wind action determination | An entered W component can be plotted separately. Site pressures,
service/ultimate nature and complete wind combinations are pending. | https://codehub.building.govt.nz/resources/asnzs-1170-22021
AS 4100:2020 | Steel structures | Hot-rolled and structural hollow-section design | Compares actions only with entered, source-referenced
capacities. Section classification, lateral stability, combined actions, connections and full standard compliance are not automatically
established. | https://steel.org.au/resources/elibrary/resources/as-nzs-5131-as-4100-2020-update/

stiffness is supplied. Effective section, local/distortional buckling, restraint and connection design require separate verification. |
https://steel.org.au/what-we-do/focus-areas/cold-formed-light-gauge-steel/standards-and-design/

detailing review. Cleats and bolts shown as estimating provisions are not a fabrication or connection approval. |
